title: Smart and Skilled contestable training entitlement (New South Wales)
summary: From 1 January 2015 NSW funded an entitlement to subsidised training up to Certificate III at approved public or private providers.

commenced.what: Smart and Skilled entitlement funding began

direction_rationale: Entitlement funding that follows the student to any approved provider opened state training subsidies to private providers, adding suppliers and shifting share from TAFE, with a risk of low-quality entry.

industries.name: Technical and Vocational Education and Training

comparison: Staggered state entitlements 2009-2015; WA, Tasmania, ACT and NT dates not checked
confounders: VET FEE-HELP expansion (Victoria 2009, national 2012) and its 2017 replacement
National Partnership on Skills Reform funding (2012-17)

verified.notes: Date from the NSW Audit Office report on Smart and Skilled.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Training subsidies follow the student to any approved public or private provider. More providers and places can lift skills, but quality and cost control have been problems, most of all in Victoria and South Australia.

marks.reason: Opens state training subsidies to private providers, adding suppliers.
Subsidised places with student choice of provider widen access to training.
